topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing the importance, complexity, and historical context of complement.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of the complement cascade, including its general functions, naming rules, and the central importance of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three recognition pathways that drive C3 deposition and generate the threshold required for full complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms triggered by complement activation, covering opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys the distinct clinical presentations and disease risks associated with deficiencies in specific complement pathway components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens circumvent complement-mediated clearance and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in biomedical applications.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with concluding remarks and a preview of the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
